scope: Josh's currently tracked laptop and desktop inventory
method: Indicative upper-end gross sale prices for individually listed, cleaned, tested machines with accurate descriptions and chargers/accessories where applicable. These are not guaranteed sale prices and do not subtract marketplace fees, postage, returns, repairs or time.

platformStrategy.bestFor: Dubbo local laptops, desktops, iMacs and bulky systems
platformStrategy.why: Local pickup avoids freight and fees, and lets buyers inspect working systems.

platformStrategy.bestFor: Duplicate local listings and bulky computers
platformStrategy.why: Useful second local channel for Dubbo and surrounding-region buyers.

platformStrategy.bestFor: Collectible or enthusiast hardware, older ThinkPads, MacBook Air and Crosshair V parts
platformStrategy.why: A national buyer pool can matter more than local demand for unusual hardware.

importantNotes: The HP ProBook x360 435 G8 should not be advertised at the upper-end price until its previously observed high-temperature behaviour has been repaired or validated.
The Crosshair V Formula-Z system may return more money parted out because the motherboard has enthusiast/collector value.
Older Windows-unsupported laptops are capped by cheap availability of much newer refurbished business laptops.
Marketplace asking prices are not the same as completed-sale prices. These figures are deliberately presented as plausible upper-end targets, not guarantees.
A fast-sale strategy usually means accepting materially less than the maximum individual-sale total.

evidenceAnchors.observed: Exact Ryzen 5 5600U / 16 GB / 256 GB used example ended at A$289; another current used/refurbished example was listed at A$385.
evidenceAnchors.interpretation: A$350 is an upper-end target only if this unit's thermal issue is demonstrably fixed and the overall condition is strong.

evidenceAnchors.observed: Exact i3-6100U / 8 GB / 128 GB examples were listed around A$80.10 with 161 sold, A$115.58, and higher asks around A$185.
evidenceAnchors.interpretation: A$100 is a defensible local upper target without assuming the highest dealer asking price is achievable.

evidenceAnchors.observed: An 8 GB / 128 GB refurbished 2015 MacBook Air sold for A$229; current pre-owned examples also appear materially lower depending on condition.
evidenceAnchors.interpretation: The A$180–A$230 range is strongly condition-, battery- and capacity-dependent.

evidenceAnchors.observed: An exact 3.4 GHz i5 / 8 GB / 1 TB / Radeon Pro 570 4 GB Gumtree example was listed at A$450; a 24 GB example was listed at A$550.
evidenceAnchors.interpretation: A$450 is directly anchored to a close current Australian comparable.

evidenceAnchors.observed: Comparable Australian systems with i5-9400F, 16 GB RAM and GTX 1660 Super were listed around A$499–A$599.
evidenceAnchors.interpretation: This PC has a non-Super GTX 1660 but useful extra storage, so A$500–A$550 is an upper-end asking target rather than a guaranteed achieved price.

evidenceAnchors.observed: A bare Crosshair V Formula-Z without I/O shield sold around A$140 equivalent, while tested-board asks can be far higher.
evidenceAnchors.interpretation: The unusually valuable motherboard is why parting the FX-era system may beat the complete-tower price.

evidenceAnchors.observed: An exact 2.66 GHz Core 2 Duo / 4 GB / 640 GB 24-inch 2009 iMac was listed at A$149 in Australia.
evidenceAnchors.interpretation: A$120–A$150 is consistent with a close Australian asking-price anchor, subject to condition and local pickup demand.
